trajectory_summary: The call opens flat, briefly warms when the customer shares his long-standing solar interest and an unprompted personal medical story, but stalls hard at the credit qualifier when the customer self-reports low credit. The rep never anchors a bill, never books a time, and closes with a vague 'text me and let me know' handoff — the call ends in drift, partly driven by the customer's own tangents into politics.
outcome_dispute: The call did not produce any appointment, booked or tentative — it ended on an open-ended 'check your credit and text me' non-commitment. This should be tagged no_appointment (bordering on a soft dq given the customer self-reported below-threshold credit), not a callback with a real commitment, since no date/time or callback window was set.

The customer self-reports being below the 650 threshold the rep just quoted. Per the schema's own policy-question note (spencer_operator_note), stated credit is unreliable — three-bureau variance is common, and a customer's self-assessment of 'not that high' isn't a hard data point. The rep treats this as an effective soft-DQ and shifts to a passive 'check and text me' loop rather than keeping the appointment alive.
